# apollo_graph_api_key (Resource)

Manages a GraphOS graph-scoped API key. The `key` value is only visible when GraphOS creates the key, so this resource stores that sensitive value in Terraform state for Terraform-created resources and intentionally cannot rehydrate it on import or refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apollo_graph_api_key" "ci" {
  graph_id = "inventory"
  name     = "inventory-ci"
  role     = "GRAPH_ADMIN"
}

import {
  to = apollo_graph_api_key.ci
  id = "inventory:graph-key-123"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `graph_id` (String) Graph identifier that owns the API key.
- `name` (String) Display name for the API key.
- `role` (String) GraphOS role to assign when creating the key. GraphOS does not allow changing roles after creation, so Terraform replaces the resource when this value changes.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when GraphOS created the API key.
- `id` (String) Remote GraphOS API key identifier. Import format: `graph_id:key_id`.
- `key` (String, Sensitive) Sensitive API key value returned by GraphOS only at creation time. Imported resources and refreshes do not rehydrate this field.
- `last_used_at` (String) Timestamp when GraphOS last observed this API key being used, when available.

## Import

Import an existing graph API key with its owning graph identifier and remote key ID:

```terraform
import {
  to = apollo_graph_api_key.ci
  id = "inventory:graph-key-123"
}
```

## Permissions

- Read, import, refresh, create, update, and delete require Org Admin or Graph Admin access for graph API key management.

## Secret Handling

- GraphOS only returns the `key` value when it creates the API key.
- Terraform stores that sensitive value in state for resources it creates.
- Imported resources and later refreshes intentionally leave `key` unset because GraphOS does not re-expose it.
